anchors.paper_title: Transcranial focused ultrasound modulates spiking, LFP, and BOLD activity in the primate thalamus
anchors.reason: The dataset README names this Zheng et al. Nat Commun paper as the publication the data support. It reports the macaque VPL FUS electrophysiology recordings, with matching authors and a matching title.

metadata.methods_description: Recordings used a NeuroNexus V1x32-Edge single-shank probe (32 sites, 100 µm pitch) in right-hemisphere VPL, acquired with a Blackrock Cerebus/CerePlex system at 30 kHz for spikes and 1 kHz for LFP. FUS was applied to VPL or insular cortex, and tactile stimulation was delivered to the contralateral hand. Raw Blackrock files were read with NPMK in MATLAB and exported to NWB using MatNWB.

citation_details.title: Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Biophysical Mechanisms, Neural Effects, and Clinical Translation
citation_details.author: Li Min Chen, Bin He, Joshua Kosnoff, Wynn Legon, Shy Shoham
citation_details.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulation technology capable of targeting both cortical and deep brain structures with millimeter-scale spatial precision. Recent advances in ultrasound hardware, acoustic modeling, neuronavigation, and multimodal imaging have accelerated the field from proof-of-concept demonstrations toward mechanistic investigation and early clinical translation. In parallel, growing evidence from animal and human studies has begun to clarify how ultrasound influences neural activity across cellular, circuit, and systems levels. In this review, we synthesize recent progress in understanding the biophysical mechanisms, neurophysiological effects, and network-level consequences of TUS.
